sources.citation: P. W. Anderson, Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass, Physical Review 130, 439 (1963).
sources.supports: The charged-condensate gauge-field mass/screening analogy underlying the Anderson-Higgs description.
sources.does_not_support: Identity between a superconducting order parameter and the Standard-Model Higgs field, or a collapse mechanism.

sources.citation: D. C. Mattis and J. Bardeen, Theory of the Anomalous Skin Effect in Normal and Superconducting Metals, Physical Review 111, 412 (1958).
sources.supports: Frequency-dependent electromagnetic response and finite surface impedance in superconductors.
sources.does_not_support: Zero impedance at all frequencies or a boundary-to-collapse transfer.

sources.citation: M. J. A. de Jong et al., Measurement of a strong nonlinear force between superconductors compatible with the Casimir force, Nature Communications 17 (2026).
sources.supports: A measured superconducting boundary-force response and a public component-replay benchmark.
sources.does_not_support: The proposed cavity response, transported covariance, DP collapse, or a Higgs-to-Casimir mechanism.

sources.citation: D. M. Harber et al., Measurement of the Casimir-Polder Force through Center-of-Mass Oscillations of a Bose-Einstein Condensate, Physical Review A 72, 033610 (2005).
sources.supports: BEC center-of-mass coherence as a surface-force sensing platform.
sources.does_not_support: Reuse of the effective Gaussian sphere DP source or a condensate-to-collapse transfer law.

sources.citation: P. W. Higgs, Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons, Physical Review Letters 13, 508 (1964).
sources.supports: The relativistic gauge-theory mass mechanism used for the Standard-Model Higgs sector.
sources.does_not_support: A superconducting material response, Casimir modifier, or Diósi collapse kernel.
